text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.3 percent this year and inflation will decrease to the level of 16.3 percent, the Gdansk-based Market Economy Research Institute said.

- Japan's Isuzu concern has confirmed its decision to invest 380 million marks in the diesel engine plant to be constructed in Tychy, southern Poland, the Polish Foreign Investment Agency (PAIZ) said.
- The Warsaw-based Prospan chipboard maker has received the International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9002 quality certificate, awarded by the Germanischer Lloyd Certification GmbH, Prospan said.

- The Gdansk Refinery (RG) in cooperation with the Polimex Cekop foreign trade firm has contracted the U.S.-based Parsons firm to construct the refinery's sulphur depositing facility worth $10 million, RG's spokesperson Ewa Sielicka said.

- The listed Exbud construction firm bought a 75 percent stake in the Przembud industrial construction firm in a tender called by the treasury ministry in January, the ministry's privatisation department deputy director Bozena Latuch said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Foreign investments in Poland, each exceeding $1 million, totalled $5.2 billion in 1996, PAIZ president Waldemar Dabrowski said.

- Polish banking sector's computerisation resulted in the introduction of 700,000 pay cards and 300,000 credit cards by the country's banks, the Komputer Expo'97 international software fair organisers said.
- The Viscoplast band-aid maker had sales of 45.1 million zlotys netting 1.8 million zlotys in 1996. The company is planning a listing on the Warsaw bourse this year.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The number of PZU-Life insurance firm's customers shrank from 17.8 million to 16.2 million last year, benefitting mostly Commercial Union and Amplico Life.
- The Warsaw-based Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK), to be privatised in April, plans to earn a gross profit of 420 million zlotys this year, PBK's forecast said.
ZYCIE

- The Hetman National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 15 plans to create a construction holding which will include construction firms and producers of cement and mineral materials controlled by Hetman, its president Krzysztof Sedzikowski said.
PARKIET

- The Katowice-province court of appeal has upheld the provincial court's verdict, which ruled the state treasury to repay of 169.36 million zlotys plus interests to the Rafamet mechanical engineering firm.

- The Piast National Investment Fund (NFI)-12 has never planned to purchase a 25 percent stake in the Prochnik garment maker and thus it had nothing to report to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW), the Fund's president Ryszard Zagorny said. Accusations of breaking the reporting requirements by Piast published by the media were false, Zagorny said.
